text:
elaine: Heads up — we're seeing weird token accounting for a subset of requests routed through the empirical-routing policy. Customers report spikes in "tokens_consumed" on the console without matching request volume.
sam: Which bucket? per-key or per-org?
elaine: per-key. Affected keys have burst enabled. Example: user sends 1 prompt + 2 tool calls + a final completion. Dashboard shows prompt + completion + tool calls = correct, but billing shows extra ~1.5x tokens on some runs.
marcus: Do we have a repro? sample request bodies?
elaine: Pasted an obfuscated trace from one run: ```json
{"key_id":"k_ABC","model":"redwood-xl-4k","prompt_tokens":128,"completion_tokens":256,"tool_calls":[{"name":"search","tokens":40}],"retries":1}```
jaya: Wait "retries":1 — are retries being double-counted? We had a change that increments token_meter on both initial and retry responses while the retry shares the same completion tokens due to idempotent rerun.
sam: I remember a guard to dedupe retries by request_id for quota enforcement, but it was only applied at the per-org aggregator, not per-key. If per-key path uses a different fast-path, we may be adding tokens twice.
marcus: Also check toolcall attribution. Tool responses may be recorded as separate RPCs that go through the meterer twice when routed across region boundary.
elaine: Example from logs: 
```
[meter] key=k_ABC inc prompt=128
[router] route -> eu-west (fallback)
[tool] call -> search returned 40
[meter] key=k_ABC inc tool=40
[retry] triggered for completion
[meter] key=k_ABC inc completion=256
[completion] sent
[meter] key=k_ABC inc completion=256  <-- duplicate
```
sam: That last line looks like the fast-path mistakenly re-applied voucher accounting on completion when a retry cleared a pending marker.
jaya: Could be race between the retry-idempotency token (in redis) and the meter checkpoint write. If the retry check races, both attempts will pass the "not yet billed" check and both will bill.
marcus: We should look at the code in infra/metering/per_key_meter.go — IIRC there are two code paths: synchronous increment for low-latency path and async batch writer. The batch writer was supposed to ignore entries with same request_id.
elaine: Quick mitigation idea: mark tool-calls as "embedded" tokens attached to parent request so they are only accounted once at finalization. But that's a behavior change and might affect historical counting.
sam: Short-term: disable fast-path for keys with burst enabled and route through authoritative per-key path that enforces request_id dedupe. That'll raise latency slightly but avoids double billing.
jaya: Agree for a short emergency patch. We should also add a Prom alert for duplicate meter increments: detect same key/request_id increment >1 within 2s.
marcus: Also add an audit log that emits request_id -> meter events so we can replay and reconcile.
elaine: Who can own the emergency rollback? Sam can flip the flag. Marcus can send a quick patch to add the retry dedupe guard to the fast-path; Jaya can add the Prom rule.
sam: I'll schedule the flag flip now, will run in prod for a couple hours then we'll monitor.
quota-bot: [automated] Feature flag "fast_path_per_key_burst" toggled OFF by sam at 2025-10-05T14:12:30Z :wrench:
elaine: Added a one-off console dashboard widget: "per-key duplicate meter events" that looks at meter_logs for >1 increments per request_id. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/QUOTA/duplicate-meter?org=platform
jaya: For long-term, propose we unify metering to the authoritative path and implement idempotent token increments at storage layer (single Redis LUA that returns whether increment applied). That way both sync and async paths call same primitive.
marcus: Also need tests: unit test for toolcall+retry scenario, integration test with routing fallback across regions, and tariff test for burst enabled keys.
sam: I'll open a short-lived epic and assign tasks. ETA for fix + tests is 48h.
elaine: Customer-facing: Ops will send a note to impacted customers saying we found a metering bug affecting some burst keys; we'll credit affected customers retroactively after reconciliation.
marcus: Good. After reconciliation, run a job to compare meter_events vs billing_export and produce diff CSV.
jaya: I'll draft the prom rule and slack alert for eng-sre.
sam: Thanks all. Keep threads short updates here.
